segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the O I Line is the central axis joining the Incenter X one and the Circumcenter X three. By Euler's formula, the squared distance between X one and X three equals R times R minus two r.

segments.text: Because the incircle and circumcircle are centered at X one and X three, both of their centers of similitude—the insimilicenter X fifty-five and exsimilicenter X fifty-six—lie on the O I line. Furthermore, the reflection of X one across X three is the Bevan Point X forty, the circumcenter of the excentral triangle.

segments.text: Through isogonal conjugation, the Gergonne Point X seven pairs with X fifty-five and the Nagel Point X eight pairs with X fifty-seven on the O I line, uniting the tritangent and circumcircle geometries.
